title: A call again. That he now poised that it now throbbed. You hear? It throbbed, pure, purer, softly and softlier, its buzzing prongs. Longer in dying call.
html_source:
This passage seems to recall Orsino’s speech from Act 1, Scene 1 of Twelfth Night:

“That strain again, it had a dying fall.
O, it came o'er my ear like the sweet sound,
That breathes upon a bank of violets,
Stealing and giving odour.”

With its focus on the aural and its reference to flowers (echoing Bloom’s reverie above), it’s an appropriate allusion for this chapter.

 From the saloon a call came, long in dying. That was a tuningfork the tuner had that he forgot that he now struck.
